newsitem.title: INDONESIA: WTO talk dampens sales of disputed Indonesian car.
newsitem.headline: WTO talk dampens sales of disputed Indonesian car.

text.p: Controversy surrounding Indonesia's Timor national car is dampening sales of the South Korean-built vehicle as consumers doubt it has a long-term future, a company official said on Wednesday.
Richard Hendarmo, director of PT Timor Distributor Nasional, said negative reporting of events surrounding the car had retarded sales.

"If you read the papers, there are always rumours about the WTO and various others things, so that the consequence is that the customer who wants to buy, but every day continues to read the negative stories, chooses to wait," he said.

The European Union, Japan and the United States have complained to the World Trade Organisation (WTO) about the special tax break given to the Timor which makes it half the price of other cars in its class.
Bilateral talks between Indonesia and the three complaining countries are taking place in Geneva in an effort to solve the dispute before it is taken to a WTO panel.

Hendarmo told a news conference PT Timor Distributor Nasional, jointly controlled by President Suharto's youngest son Hutomo Mandala Putra and Kia Motors of South Korea, had delivered 5,800 sedans since it began public sales on October 1.

This was below the monthly target of 3,000-4,000 cars, he said. PT Timor had a "buffer stock" of 6,000 vehicles in a lot near Jakarta's main international airport, but Hendarmo could not say how many of the 1,500 cc cars had been ordered by customers.
He added that only around 40 cars had been sold to government agencies and another two were donated to the Palestinian embassy in Jakarta because of "good relations" with the mission, he said.
Hendarmo said negative reports in the local media about the company's readiness in terms of spare parts and service had created doubts in the minds of consumers.

Speaking after the official opening of the company's head office in central Jakarta, Hendarmo asked the media to report that the company already had 26 official agents on Java, Sumatra, Sulawesi and Kalimantan.
He said Timor also had a 4,000 square metre (43,000 sq foot) warehouse in East Jakarta full of spare parts.
"If you write stories that we are ready with spare parts and service then we will help each other," he said.
